study of the electronic and
magnetic properties of Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ within the framework of dynamical mean
field theory (DMFT). We employ the Hubbard model in a tight-binding model
corrected for multi-band screening and multi-orbital screening effects in the
impersonal $d$-sector. We find that the DMFT solution is only weakly
dependent on the choice of the bare model. Our results show that the
single-band $t_{2g}$-Hubbard model is a reasonable approximation for the
electronic properties of Sr$_2$RuO$_4$. We obtain a well-defined magnetic
transition at the experimental temperature, and find that the spin-flip
excitation at the M-point is of magnetic origin. The DMFT spectral function
shows a well-defined Kondo peak at the Fermi level, and the superconducting
gap function is fully gapped in the $\alpha$- or $A_{1g}$-symmetry. The
magnitude of the gap is strongly dependent on the choice of the bare model, but
the overall shape of the gap is robust. We find that the superconducting
transition temperature is of the order of 1.5 K, which is in reasonable
agreement with experiment.

are crucial to obtain a well-defined magnetic transition. We also find that the
impersonal $d$-screening effects are crucial to obtain a reasonable value for
the spin-orbit coupling. Finally, we find that the combination of multi-band
and impersonal $d$-screening effects is crucial to obtain a reasonable value
for the hybridization function at the Fermi level.

  Object Detection (OD) is a fundamental task in computer vision. Convolutional
Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved great success in OD. However, the
stability of CNNs is still a problem. We propose a novel method to stabilize
the training of CNNs for object detection. Our method is based on the
observation that the ReLU activation function is not differentiable at zero.
Thus, we propose to add a small constant to the input of the ReLU function to
make it differentiable. We show that our method is equivalent to adding a
constant to the weight of the convolutional layer. Experiments show that our
method achieves stable training and superior performance. Codes are available
at https://github.com/Chen-YuTsai/ReluStable.

networks. Our method is based on the observation that the receptive field of
the feature map is larger than the bounding box. We propose to use the feature
map outside the bounding box to improve the detection performance. We show
that our method is equivalent to adding a convolutional layer with a larger
kernel size. Experiments show that our method achieves superior performance.
Codes are available at https://github.com/Chen-YuTsai/ReceptiveField.

been widely used in the study of Galactic structure. We present a new method
for deriving the scale length of the thin disk of the Milky Way using the
infrared luminosity of the stellar populations within the solar cylinder. We
extract the infrared color index maps of the Galactic disk from the WISE data
and derive the surface brightness profiles of the thin disk in $K_s$ vs.

luminosity of the stellar populations within the solar cylinder. We find that

theory is a well-studied area of
research. In this paper, we study the upper density of the set of integers
$\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ that avoid a given pattern $P$ in the standard
subsequence ordering. We prove that for many patterns $P$ the density of such
sets is asymptotically $1 - \frac{1}{2^{|P|}}$ as $n \to \infty$. This
confirms a conjecture of Balogh, Ellis, and Sharp. We also study the upper
density of the set of integers $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ that avoid two patterns
$P_1$ and $P_2$. We prove that for many pairs of patterns $(P_1,P_2)$ the
upper density of such sets is asymptotically $1 - \frac{1}{3^{|P_1|+|P_2|}}$
as $n \to \infty$.
  We also study the problem of finding the largest possible upper density of
the set of integers $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ that avoid two patterns $P_1$ and
$P_2$ with the additional property that $P_1$ and $P_2$ are comparable in
the standard subsequence ordering. We prove that for many pairs of patterns
$(P_1,P_2)$ the largest possible upper density of such sets is asymptotically
$1 - \frac{1}{2^{|P_1|} + |P_2|}$ as $n \to \infty$.
  The proofs of the results in this paper use a new and general approach to
upper density problems in Ramsey theory. This approach was developed by the
first and second authors in \cite{BLS}, and it has already been used to solve
many other problems in this area of research.
  We also introduce a new notation for describing patterns in the standard
subsequence ordering. This notation is more convenient than the standard
notation used in the literature, and it simplifies many of the arguments in
this paper.
  Finally, we note that the results in this paper are part of a larger program
to study the relationship between Ramsey theory and extremal combinatorics.

  We report on the implementation of a quantum spatial search algorithm in a
network of 5 qubits. The search is performed in a graph with 16 vertices,
which is encoded in the qubits using a combination of superpositions and
entanglements. The algorithm is implemented in two different scenarios: one in
which the graph is encoded in the qubits before the search, and another in
which the graph is constructed during the search. In both cases, we observe a
clear enhancement of the search efficiency due to quantum interference. We
also show that the quantum search is robust against errors in the qubits'
rotations, which are induced by decoherence. Our results demonstrate the
potential of quantum search algorithms for the development of quantum
technologies in networks of qubits.

search engines are designed to provide relevant information in response to
queries, they can also be used to spread misinformation and propaganda. In
particular, search engines can be exploited to spread conspiracy theories and
fake news. In this paper, we focus on the problem of detecting fake news
propaganda in search engines. We propose a novel framework that leverages
graph-based methods to model the structure of search engine results pages (SERPs)
and then uses this structure to detect fake news propaganda. We develop a
novel algorithm that combines the structure of the graph with the content of the
links it contains to detect fake news propaganda. We evaluate our approach on
two datasets of SERPs and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

conspiracy theories in search engines.

each edge in $S$ is removed independently with probability $q$. We study the
asymptotic behavior of the expected degree of the remaining vertices of $G$ as
$n\to\infty$, as well as the distribution of the remaining degree of a
typical vertex of $G$. We also study the distribution of the number of vertices
with a remaining degree greater than or equal to $d$.

for $\deg(v)$ of order $\sqrt{n}$. For the distribution of the remaining
degree of a typical vertex, we obtain an asymptotic expression for the
probability that a typical vertex has a remaining degree $d$ as $n\to\infty$ for
$d$ of order $\sqrt{n}$. We also study the distribution of the number of
vertices with a remaining degree greater than or equal to $d$. We obtain an
asymptotic expression for the probability that a fraction $\alpha$ of vertices
have a remaining degree greater than or equal to $d$ as $n\to\infty$ for $d$ of
order $\sqrt{n}$.

against edge removals. We believe that our results will be useful in the study

framework that simultaneously reconstructs the intensity and density maps of
the object from a single image of a foggy object. The proposed framework
consists of two cascaded networks: a density map estimation network and an
intensity map estimation network. The density map estimation network estimates
the density map from the intensity map, and the intensity map estimation network
reconstructs the intensity map from the intensity map estimated by the previous
network. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework through
both qualitative and quantitative experiments.

network to simultaneously estimate the density and intensity maps. The
variant framework is obtained by adding a density estimation sub-network to the
previous framework. We show that the variant framework outperforms a
state-of-the-art deep learning framework that simultaneously estimates the
density and intensity maps.

for modeling long
sequential data. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are a primary example of
recurrent structures, which are widely used for modeling and processing
sequential data. However, RNNs are known to suffer from the vanishing
gradient problem, which limits their ability to model long-range dependencies
in sequential data. In this paper, we propose a novel recurrent structure that
can model long sequential data of unlimited length. Our proposed structure
avoids the vanishing gradient problem by using a self-modifying mechanism that
updates the recurrent state in a way that is controlled by the input data.
Moreover, our proposed structure is a universal approximator, which means that
it can approximate any function with arbitrary precision. We demonstrate the
effectiveness of our proposed structure on the task of modeling the
multiplication of numbers represented as sequences of digits.
  We experiment with two different implementations of our proposed structure:
one based on a neural network and another based on a program. Our experiments
show that it can learn to multiply numbers of up to 13 digits with high
accuracy. We also show that our proposed structure can learn to model
sequential data of unlimited length by learning to extend its own state.
Finally, we show that our proposed structure can learn to model complex
sequential data that contains multiple interacting components.

regression problem and propose a novel end-to-end framework that takes the 2D

novel loss function that is able to effectively minimize the reprojection

state-of-the-art methods.

art methods. Our code and dataset are available online at

omatic, bicategorical framework for
generalizing topological Hochschild homology (THH) to arbitrary bicategories.
In this paper, we show that the bicategory of commutative algebraic theories
(known as the bicategory of varieties) and the bicategory of symmetric monoidal
categories are each equivalent to the bicategory of shadows. As a consequence,
we obtain two functors from each of these bicategories to the theory of shadows.
We show that THH factors through these equivalences, providing a new
interpretation of shadowing in terms of the Hochschild structure inherent in
THH. We also show that the functor from algebraic theories to shadows preserves
universal properties, and that the shadow of an algebraic theory encodes its
universal properties in a way that is analogous to how its presentation by
generators and relations encodes its algebraic properties.
  Finally, we show that the shadow of a symmetric monoidal category is
equivalent to its THH with coefficients in the category. This provides a
generalization of the result that THH of a commutative ring is equivalent to
its THH with coefficients in the ring.

original graph. We show that finding a minimum positive spanning subgraph is

with a specific coloring of the vertices, finding a minimum positive spanning
subgraph is equivalent to finding a minimum weight perfect matching. We
establish NP-hardness of finding a minimum positive spanning subgraph for
signed bipartite graphs even when the edges are colored using only two colors.

positive spanning subgraph can be done in pseudo-polynomial time. We also show
